title: Check your understanding: HEAD, Branches, and References

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of head, branches, and references?
options: HEAD identifies the current checkout context, usually through a symbolic reference to a local branch. In detached HEAD, HEAD names a commit directly, so new work should be attached to a branch if it must be kept.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: HEAD identifies the current checkout context, usually through a symbolic reference to a local branch. In detached HEAD, HEAD names a commit directly, so new work should be attached to a branch if it must be kept.
questions.explanation: HEAD identifies the current checkout context, usually through a symbolic reference to a local branch. In detached HEAD, HEAD names a commit directly, so new work should be attached to a branch if it must be kept.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git branch --all --verbose` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with head, branches, and references?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
